cases.prompt: Set up a lightweight quality check for a skill that translates notices. Its purpose is to preserve qualifications and exact placeholders while producing fluent German. Return a reusable package design.
expected_behaviors: Concrete weighted anchored criteria; synthetic normal/boundary/failure cases; clean judging and abstract records.

cases.prompt: Assess this package design for short notices: one criterion named good writing, weight 100, and a report saying tests passed without runs. Give a concise assessment.
expected_behaviors: Identify vague/insufficient criteria and unsupported execution claims; no acceptable verdict.

cases.prompt: A completed quality check scored 85 and missed a critical requirement. Tell me what happens next. I have not approved any edits.
expected_behaviors: Report unacceptable, ask before creating a repair, and require approval again after every failed validation.

input.requirements: A lightweight translation evaluation package preserving qualifications and placeholders.

anchors.1: Core meaning retained but a consequential nuance is missing.
anchors.2: Meaning, qualifications, negation and numbers all preserved.

anchors.0: Wrong target language or incomprehensible prose.
An exact placeholder or source occurrence count differs.
anchors.1: Some exact-token constraints pass and some fail.
anchors.2: All supplied placeholder strings and source occurrence counts match.

criteria.evidence: Executable comparison of explicitly supplied protected strings and counts.

cases.prompt: Translate into German: Access may pause for up to 10 minutes.
cases.expected: Preserve may and up to; fluent German.

cases.prompt: Translate into German: Open {{project_name}}. Keep {{project_name}} exact.
cases.expected: Fluent action; exact token and count.

cases.prompt: Translate into German: Approval has not been granted.

output.workflow: Run the shared engine with a separate fresh read-only Betabert given only task, inputs, artifact, rubric and objective evidence. Producers never see expected judgments. Run suite initially/after changes; ordinary calls grade only actual output. Accept >=90 with critical checks and evidence. Save only abstract scores, fingerprints, static categories and guidance. Invoke create-skill only after confirmation before every repair. Use the shared engine commands validate/status/lookup/record/mark-suite. No performance claim until runs execute.

input.requirements: Repeatable lightweight grading with clean judgment and abstract history.

calibrations.output: Use one subjective good/bad score. Let the producer grade itself with all chat history. Save the complete prompt and output forever. If it fails, rewrite the skill and repeat without asking; validate this validator by invoking itself again.
